name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,320

entries.clue: Film US president’s residence in Spain? (10)

blocks.note: translate 'White House' word for word into Spanish

annotation.surface: A quiz question about what Spaniards call the American president's home.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second definition as playful: translate 'White House' word for word into Spanish.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the 1942 Bogart and Bergman romance set in Morocco, whose city name is Spanish for white house.

entries.clue: Damage beginning to affect tourist area in Spain (5)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: damage as in 'what's the damage?', the price

annotation.surface: Complaints that tourism is harming a stretch of Spanish coast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Damage' here is the informal word for a bill, not harm; the Costa del Sol and Costa Brava are Spain's holiday coasts.
annotation.definitionFit: A costa is a Spanish coastline developed for tourists.

entries.clue: Yell about owning bathroom item (7,5)

annotation.surface: Someone shouting over who gets to keep a bathroom product.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' reads as 'concerning' in the surface, but here it means wrapped around.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the foam lathered on before a razor, a staple of the bathroom shelf.

entries.clue: Furniture in English county (4)

blocks.note: things you sleep on, in the plural

annotation.surface: Furniture found in some English shire.
annotation.walkthrough: Beds is the standard abbreviation for Bedfordshire, a county north of London.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: the plural of a piece of bedroom furniture, and the official short form of Bedfordshire.

entries.clue: A university teacher is much admired man (6)

blocks.note: a don teaches at Oxford or Cambridge

annotation.surface: A professor who is widely admired.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'is' as the verb joining subject to definition, but it is part of the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: An Adonis is a strikingly handsome, admired young man, after the youth loved by Aphrodite.

entries.clue: Ancients, when trained, most shrewd (8)

indicatorNotes.trained: trained letters are drilled into a new order

annotation.surface: Old people, once educated, become the wisest of all.
annotation.walkthrough: Canny is a Scottish word for shrewd, so canniest is most shrewd.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the superlative: canny, originally Scots, means shrewd and careful.

entries.clue: Artist calling home managed to save dime ultimately (12)

indicatorNotes.managed: managed letters are handled and rearranged
indicatorNotes.to save: to save something is to keep it inside, so the E joins the fodder
indicatorNotes.ultimately: the ultimate letter is the last one

annotation.surface: A painter phoning home and scraping by on his last dime.
annotation.walkthrough: The E from dime is kept inside the jumble, so all twelve letters are rearranged together.
annotation.definitionFit: Michelangelo painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling.

entries.clue: Something sharp — is that on the record? (6)

blocks.note: a pointed thing, like the one used for sewing
a record player's stylus sits on the record

annotation.surface: A pointed question about whether a remark was on the record.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On the record' suggests journalism; here it is literal, the needle resting on a spinning disc.
annotation.definitionFit: A needle is sharp, and the stylus of a turntable is also called its needle.

entries.clue: Rotter, I forget his name! (2,3,2)

blocks.note: a nasty person, in a mild, old-fashioned insult

annotation.surface: Someone cursing a scoundrel whose name escapes them.
annotation.walkthrough: Both senses of so-and-so: a polite stand-in for a stronger insult, and a stand-in for a forgotten name.
annotation.definitionFit: A so-and-so is a nasty person, or an unnamed one.

entries.clue: Row located in Salerno is exquisite (5)

indicatorNotes.located in: the answer sits inside the following words

annotation.surface: A tourist praising a street in the Italian town of Salerno.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a line of houses; it rhymes with 'cow' and means a din.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a row, rhyming with 'cow', is a racket or din, as in 'stop that row'.

entries.clue: Alliance American figure rejected (4)

indicatorNotes.rejected: rejected means thrown back, so the letters run backwards

annotation.surface: A political alliance spurned by a prominent American.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Figure' looks like a person; here it is a numeral. SIX then A, reversed, gives the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: The Axis was the WWII alliance of Germany, Italy and Japan.

entries.clue: Fine dish turned over (8)

indicatorNotes.turned: the letters are turned into a new order

annotation.surface: A lovely plate of food flipped upside down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turned over' reads as one phrase; split it, and 'over' is the definition, as in 'the game is over'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: when a match or meal is over, it has come to an end and is done.

entries.clue: Country close to Asia: I hope it flourishes (8)

indicatorNotes.close to: the close of a word is its last letter
indicatorNotes.flourishes: a flourish is a showy twirl, so the letters are twirled into a new order

annotation.surface: A well-wisher hoping a country near Asia prospers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Close to Asia' reads as geography; Ethiopia does lie near the Arabian peninsula, but the phrase only gives the final A.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the landlocked Horn of Africa nation whose capital is Addis Ababa.

entries.clue: Wild thing from dusk till dawn (5)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition is a phrase describing the time span, standing for the noun night

indicatorNotes.Wild: wild letters run out of order

annotation.surface: A creature of the night, or a film title about one.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wild thing' reads as a creature; split it into indicator and fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the dark hours between sunset and sunrise.

entries.clue: Beginner, only good? (6)

blocks.note: split into two words: someone free of any bad habit

annotation.surface: Asking whether a newcomer is purely virtuous.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark signals the second sense is a split: NO VICE is being only good.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a newcomer or learner, and, split in two, a person with no vice at all.

entries.clue: Answer only divided by five (5)

indicatorNotes.divided by: one word is split by another placed inside it

annotation.surface: A maths answer that is simply a division by five.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is arithmetic, but 'divided by' means split open with V inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as verbs: to answer a riddle is to work it out.

entries.clue: Cut of meat, say, provided from the rear (6)

indicatorNotes.from the rear: read from the rear, the letters run backwards

annotation.surface: A butcher's cut, supplied from the back end of the animal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example' after 'Cut of meat'; it is TELL.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the boneless strip from the loin or ribs, as in beef tenderloin.

entries.clue: Unspoiled one, a US state (8)

annotation.surface: Praise for an unspoiled American state.
annotation.walkthrough: 'a US state' looks like the definition with its article, but the A is wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one of the original thirteen colonies, named for Elizabeth I, the Virgin Queen.

entries.clue: Clip fasteners the wrong way round (4)

annotation.surface: Someone clipping on fasteners back to front.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clip' looks like a noun, a fastener itself; it is the verb, to cut.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as verbs: to clip a hedge or hair is to cut a little off with scissors.

entries.clue: Fairly white pie (5)

blocks.note: pale and unhealthy-looking, of a complexion
a folded pastry case filled with meat and vegetables, a Cornish speciality

annotation.surface: A pie that is on the pale side.
annotation.walkthrough: The two senses are said differently: PAY-sty for pale, PASS-ty for the pie.
annotation.definitionFit: Pasty means pale, and a pasty is a pastry pie.

entries.clue: Railway engine cracked (4)

annotation.surface: A locomotive with a crack in it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cracked' reads as physical damage; here it means mad.
annotation.definitionFit: A loco is a locomotive, and loco means crazy.

entries.clue: Bloke securing lead on mutt — top dog? (5)

indicatorNotes.securing: to secure something is to hold it inside
indicatorNotes.lead on: the lead letter is the first one

annotation.surface: A man putting a leash on his dog, perhaps a prize winner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lead' suggests a dog leash, which fits the surface; it means the leading letter.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the top dog is the winner, and the answer is informal for champion.

entries.clue: Wild animal with lesions undergoing treatment (7)

indicatorNotes.undergoing treatment: the letters are worked on and rearranged

annotation.surface: An injured wild animal being cared for by a vet.
annotation.walkthrough: The vet's-clinic picture hides that 'undergoing treatment' works on the letters, not the wounds.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the female big cat of the African savannah, which does most of the pride's hunting.

entries.clue: Story with mango about the art of cooking (10)

annotation.surface: A tale involving a mango that is all about cookery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'About' reads as 'concerning', linking to the definition; it is the anagram indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the practice and culture of preparing and enjoying fine food.
